claim: All three commissioned reports arrived during synthesis after a ~20 minute poll (R1_AUTONOMY.md 47442 B, R2_COORDINATES.md 37301 B, R3_UI.md 34557 B) and are fully incorporated. Records prefixed PROJECT-topic (FW/ODO/FUS/CRD/NAV/LID/MIS/UI/OPS) come from the project's own measured facts; records prefixed R1/R2/R3 come from the external reports. Where they conflict, the project record is marked OVERRIDE and wins.
why: Provenance must stay separable: the project's records were measured on this rover, the reports' records were researched from public sources. A later agent must be able to tell which is which without re-reading the reports. Spot-checks: R2's repo citations (LIDAR_FIX_ENABLED at fpms_odom_tf.py:583, wall_fit/manhattan_offset/arena_fix_from_scan/map_to_odom_from_fix, TRACK_M/MM_PER_TICK) and R3's UI citations (assumed hex, ABORT render condition) were verified line-by-line and were accurate, with one stale exception (R3-003).

claim: Cloudflare Vectorize is NOT a binding in this project's Workers. Verified by reading both wrangler files: cloud/cloudapp/wrangler.jsonc binds AI, HUB (Durable Object), DB (D1 fpms-history), ASSETS; cloud/dashboard/gateway/wrangler.toml binds FPMS_KV only. A repo-wide grep for 'vectorize' returns nothing.
why: The synthesis brief asserted Vectorize was already bound. It is not. Standing up a vector store here would be NEW infrastructure (index creation, an embedding model, an ingest path), not the flip of an existing switch. This corrects the premise the 'stream research into a vector DB' request rested on.

claim: The drive firmware's velocity loop regulates INTEGER encoder counts per 10 ms PID period. One count per period = 0.0145 m/s on the wire. Below that the setpoint is under a single count and feedback is pure quantisation noise. Measured: 0.0041 wire = 0.28 counts = stalls then lurches; 0.012 = 0.83 counts = noise; 0.100 = 6.9 counts = clean and correct.
why: This is the single most load-bearing hardware fact in the project. It is the reason 'just command a slower speed' is not available, and it OVERRIDES any external source that recommends low continuous velocities for precision. It is quantisation, not tuning — PID gains cannot fix it. The real fix is the encoder/wheel constants, i.e. a firmware rebuild.

claim: PWM_MOTOR_DEAD_ZONE is 200 of a 400-tick scale — a 50% duty FEED-FORWARD. Commanded duty is either exactly 0 or 50-100%. There is no gentle duty on this chassis.
why: Amplitude buys nothing. Any published technique whose 'slow' depends on a small continuous setpoint produces stall-then-lurch here, not slow motion. This is the mechanism behind FW-001's observed behaviour.

claim: Slow is bought with TIME, not amplitude. Measured wheels-off: wire 0.00295 (10% of cruise) = no motion at all; wire 0.0295 (cruise) = violent; pulse 0.25 s = no motion; pulse 0.35 s = MOVES, ~0.18 per pulse. Minimum pulse that moves anything is ~0.35 s.
why: The only available lever for fine positioning is pulse width with full stops between pulses. Note 0.35 s is LONGER than the 0.075-0.17 s the prior golden code used, because that code commanded raw duty (instant torque) while this commands a velocity setpoint a PID must converge to. CRITICAL CAVEAT: every number here is FREE-SPINNING, wheels off, and must be re-measured under load before being trusted for distance.

claim: Firmware passes linear.x 1:1 to wheel m/s with no gain, yet commanding 0.10 yields ~0.61 m/s actual (~6x). The fitted hardware does not match the firmware constants (MOTOR_ENCODER_CIRCLE 1040 counts/rev, MOTOR_WHEEL_CIRCLE 150.8 mm) — most likely x4 quadrature decoding plus a wheel/gear difference.
why: Every wire-value-to-real-world conversion in the project carries this unresolved ~6x factor. Any distance or speed figure must state which side of it it is on. Fixing the constants is the same firmware rebuild that would fix FW-001.

claim: CONSEQUENCE OF FW-001..004: stable control needs >= ~0.0145 m/s wire ~= 0.09 m/s real, and with margin ~0.18 m/s. 'Very slow' below that is physically unavailable. 'Slow and controlled' on this hardware means short bounded segments with full stops between them, run at a speed the loop can actually hold.
why: This is the design rule every mission, controller and UI affordance on this rover must obey. It is the single sentence to hand any future agent or external-source comparison.

claim: /odom_raw twist.linear.x is SIGN-INVERTED relative to its own pose.position. Measured wheels-off: cmd +0.012 -> twist -0.842, pose +1.395 (forward); cmd +0.100 -> twist -1.225, pose +3.505 (forward); cmd -0.012 -> twist +0.574, pose -1.506 (backward); cmd 0 -> both 0 (agree). TRUST POSE. NEVER TRUST TWIST.
why: This one fault produced a phantom 'the chassis lurches' theory, a phantom deadband floor, a safety guard wired exactly backwards, and a retracted '290 mm backward lurch' conclusion. Any guard comparing a commanded sign against reported twist fires on correct motion and stays silent on real reversal. ODOM_TWIST_SIGN = -1 is the single point of correction.

claim: 'Trust pose' must include the SIGN, not just the magnitude. Taking distance from hypot(dx,dy) and direction from twist is still a twist read in front of a direction decision. Get the sign from the pose by projecting the delta onto the board's own reported yaw FROM THE SAME MESSAGE: along = dx*cos(board_yaw) + dy*sin(board_yaw).
why: Both fields come from one message, so the projection is internally consistent whatever the board's frame is doing. If orientation is identity this degenerates to dx — exactly the signed quantity ODO-001's table was read from, so the identity case IS the measured case. Implemented in fpms_teleop.py _on_odom/summarize_leg and fpms_odom_tf.py travel_sign().

claim: hypot() is unsigned, so a 'no directional evidence -> assume forward' fallback turns a parked rover's position noise into a monotonic forward creep. With no evidence the honest displacement is ZERO.
why: This is a silent dead-reckoning error source that accumulates while the rover is not even moving. It is the kind of bug that only shows up as 'the rover thinks it has drifted across the arena overnight'.

claim: Twist is retained as a corroborating witness with NO authority: it is compared against the pose verdict and disagreements are COUNTED and logged. Genuinely ambiguous projections fall back to twist and are counted separately.
why: That counter is the cheapest test that would catch the firmware being fixed (or breaking differently) without anybody re-running a bench sweep. If the firmware is ever fixed, flipping ODOM_TWIST_SIGN to +1 is the entire fix.

claim: OPEN CONTRADICTION, NOBODY HAS CHECKED: is /odom_raw pose.pose.orientation a real encoder-derived yaw or the identity quaternion? fpms_teleop.py _on_odom says 'the board publishes an identity orientation'; its summarize_leg says 'odom yaw is dead-reckoned from the wheels'. These cannot both be true.
why: One `ros2 topic echo /odom_raw --once` after a turn settles it. It is prerequisite #1 for enabling the complementary heading filter in fpms_odom_tf.py, whose time constant is deliberately None until this is resolved. fpms_odom_tf.py logs which it observed at startup and is correct either way.

claim: Re-zero the origin after EVERY boot. The origin file survives reboots but the board's odometry restarts at 0, so a stale reference once put the rover at (-9182, -11926) mm inside a 1200 mm arena — and it plans confidently from that.
why: A coordinate-frame error of this size is not subtle in its cause but is completely silent in its symptom: every downstream component behaves correctly against a wrong origin. Cheapest possible check, catastrophic if skipped.

claim: /imu orientation is NOT fused by the board firmware — the quaternion is identity (0,0,0,1) on every message, at ~25 Hz. Heading must be INTEGRATED from angular_velocity.z.
why: Reading the quaternion and expecting a bearing yields a robot that believes it is permanently facing +x. Any external source that assumes a fused AHRS quaternion from the IMU does not apply here.

claim: Fusion strategy: position from wheel odometry (pose deltas), heading from integrated gyro Z. This is exactly the combination the rover's prior working code used, which measured 0.6% distance error and +/-1-4 degrees on turns. It is deliberately not more clever than that.
why: This is the project's measured accuracy budget and the baseline any proposed fusion upgrade must beat. 0.6% over a 1.2 m arena is ~7 mm — already well inside the 100 mm xy_goal_tolerance configured in Nav2.

claim: The dominant error term in a gyro-integrated heading is the gyro Z BIAS. It is estimated while stationary (a settling window at startup, then continuously re-estimated whenever commanded velocity is zero and wheel motion is ~0) and subtracted before integration.
why: Bias estimation is what makes an unbounded-drift sensor usable over a mission-length window. The segment-and-stop motion strategy forced by FW-005 conveniently supplies frequent stationary windows to re-estimate in — the two design constraints reinforce each other.

claim: Heading is GYRO ONLY, unconditionally, and that is a deliberate documented choice. Gyro Z drifts without bound at the residual bias rate but has NO slip mechanism — a rate gyro measures the body's actual rotation whatever the wheels do. Encoder/wheel yaw has bounded per-turn error but on THIS 4WD skid-steer chassis is systematically wrong by an UNMEASURED scale factor, and the error is large.
why: A skid-steer has no steering: every degree of yaw is produced by dragging four wheels sideways across the floor, so the encoder-inferred (v_right - v_left)/TRACK carries an effective-track slip factor nobody has measured. This is the strongest reason to distrust any external source that fuses wheel yaw into heading on a differential-drive assumption. The complementary filter is written but its time constant stays None until two named measurements exist; encoder yaw is accumulated as a cross-check and reported every 30 s.

claim: Arena is 1200 x 1200 mm. World origin BOTTOM-LEFT, +x right, +y up, millimetres. Rover starts BOTTOM-RIGHT facing forward = 90 degrees (up the arena).
why: Single source of truth for arena geometry is frontend/src/lib/arena.ts, where ARENA_MM = 1200 and every zone, grid pitch, wall threshold and start pose is a FRACTION of it, so changing one number rescales the map coherently.

claim: Four frames are in play: world (origin bottom-left, +y UP, mm); canvas (origin top-left, +y DOWN, CSS px); body (rover-fixed, origin at the LiDAR, +x out the nose, +y to port, mm); and heading psi in radians CCW from world +x. worldToCanvasY is the ONE place in the entire frontend where the y flip happens.
why: Concentrating the flip in one function means every other module — clusterer, renderer, zone table — works in world millimetres and never thinks about screen orientation. If the map ever renders mirrored, that function is the only place to look. Also: canvas rotation is clockwise-positive while psi is CCW-positive, so any ctx.rotate() with a heading must negate it — rotate(-psi).

claim: The LD06 LiDAR reports angles increasing CLOCKWISE while the body frame is CCW-positive, so LIDAR_ANGLE_SIGN = -1. LIDAR_ZERO_OFFSET_DEG = 0 means bin 0 points out the nose. Bins at or fractionally under range_max (RANGE_SATURATION_FRAC = 0.995 of the 6.0 m clamp) are the driver's saturation value, NOT a real surface.
why: Negating the bin index is what puts a wall on the rover's left in the scan on the rover's left on the map. Treating a literal 6.000 as a wall paints a phantom ring at max range and swamps the clusterer — the same class of error as LID-003's 0.0-means-obstacle trap, at the other end of the range.

claim: Expected TF tree: odom -> base_footprint (DYNAMIC, /tf, fpms_odom_tf.py, ~10 Hz paced by /odom_raw) -> base_link (STATIC, /tf_static, fpms_tf.launch.py) -> {laser_frame, imu_frame} (STATIC). map -> odom is AMCL's edge and does not exist yet; until AMCL runs, odom being the tree root is expected, not a bug.
why: Nav2 fails confusingly if any link is missing. Verify every edge with tf2_echo before launching Nav2 — TF_TREE.md gives healthy and broken output for each of the 6 checks.

claim: ONE PUBLISHER PER EDGE, NO EXCEPTIONS. fpms_odom_tf.py's PUBLISH_LASER_STATIC_TF flag is now False because fpms_tf.launch.py owns the path to laser_frame via base_link. Re-enabling it while running the launch file gives laser_frame two parents and the tree stops being a tree.
why: The failure mode is deceptive: view_frames shows two disconnected-looking chains, or tf2_echo reports wildly inconsistent numbers that change depending on which broadcaster most recently won the race. Not an error message — just wrong numbers.

claim: LiDAR and IMU mount offsets are UNMEASURED PLACEHOLDERS: base_link -> laser_frame is [0.0, 0.0, 0.065] yaw 0, base_link -> imu_frame is [0,0,0] identity. base_footprint -> base_link is [0.0, 0.0, 0.035].
why: A clean tf2_echo here proves only that the tree is CONNECTED, not that the numbers are right. Do not treat it as license to trust a map built with it. Fix: measure with a ruler from base_link (35 mm above ground, centred over the drive axle) to the LiDAR optical centre plus mount yaw, then edit the constants at the top of nav2/fpms_tf.launch.py.

claim: TF and /odom are stamped with the Pi's ROS clock, NOT the board's. Board time falls outside tf2's buffer and Nav2 rejects it with a confusing extrapolation error.
why: 'Lookup would require extrapolation into the future' is usually a clock/stamp problem, not a real gap. If that error appears now, something upstream of this guard changed.

claim: fpms_odom_tf.py's watchdog SUSPENDS the TF broadcast when /odom_raw goes stale (ODOM_STALE_SEC = 2.0), rather than repeating the last transform. Its own comment: 'A frozen TF is strictly worse than no TF'.
why: Same principle as LID-004. A consumer can detect an absent transform; it cannot detect a stale one that still looks fresh. Nav2 planning against a frozen pose is planning against a world nobody is observing.

claim: Nav2 1.1.20 is ALREADY fully installed from apt (arm64, Humble): nav2_bringup, nav2_simple_commander, nav2_amcl, nav2_costmap_2d, DWB/MPPI/Regulated-Pure-Pursuit controllers, slam_toolbox 2.6.10, robot_localization. Disk 49% of 29 G, ~15 G free. DO NOT REINSTALL.
why: Verified 2026-07-31. A reinstall attempt wastes a session and risks the working system. import nav2_simple_commander.robot_navigator already works.

claim: DO NOT import tf_transformations. It is installed correctly but fails at runtime with 'AttributeError: np.maximum_sctype was removed in the NumPy 2.0 release'. A user-local NumPy 2.x in /home/ubuntu/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/ shadows the system NumPy and is too new for the system transforms3d.
why: DO NOT fix this by changing NumPy on the rover — the camera/YOLO path in fpms-rover-agent depends on NumPy and currently works; downgrading to satisfy a convenience library risks the most reliable part of the system. Compute quaternions inline instead; for planar motion it is two lines (qz,qw = sin(yaw/2),cos(yaw/2); yaw = atan2(2(qw*qz+qx*qy), 1-2(qy^2+qz^2))). Nearly every external Nav2 tutorial imports tf_transformations, so this contradicts external sources by default.

claim: FollowPath uses RegulatedPurePursuitController with desired_linear_vel = 0.18 m/s. This is not a preference — it is the floor imposed by FW-001 with margin. At 0.18 m/s a full 1.2 m arena traverse takes 6.7 s.
why: DO NOT LOWER desired_linear_vel 'to be safe'. Lowering it below ~0.09 makes the rover LESS safe: the setpoint drops under one encoder count, the velocity loop loses feedback, and the 50% duty feed-forward turns the result into stall-then-lurch. This directly inverts the standard external advice to reduce max velocity in confined spaces.

claim: EVERY velocity taper in RPP is disabled or floored: use_regulated_linear_velocity_scaling false, use_cost_regulated_linear_velocity_scaling false, regulated_linear_scaling_min_speed 0.18, min_approach_linear_velocity 0.18 (equal to cruise, making the approach taper mathematically inert), use_velocity_scaled_lookahead_dist false.
why: Each taper would slow the rover below the firmware floor. Nav2's default min_approach_linear_velocity is 0.05 m/s — a third of the floor, i.e. guaranteed stall-then-lurch on EVERY goal approach. Cost regulation is doubly useless in a 1.2 m arena where the rover is ALWAYS near a wall, so it would pin speed at minimum permanently. Curvature regulation is off because there is no slower speed to slow to; tight turns are handled by rotate-to-heading instead.

claim: Rotate-to-heading implements the proven turn-then-drive strategy. allow_reversing and use_rotate_to_heading are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE in Nav2 — setting both true makes RPP throw on configure. Reversing is given up willingly.
why: The LiDAR only looks forward-ish and there is no rear sensing at all, so reversing under Nav2 would be blind. Note this differs from the deadreckon backend's retrace, which reverses deliberately along a path already proven clear (MIS-003).

claim: Small-arena costmap params: local costmap 0.9 x 0.9 m at 0.01 m resolution, update 5 Hz / publish 2 Hz; global costmap 2 x 2 m at 0.01 m, update and publish 1 Hz; robot_radius 0.15 m; inflation_radius 0.20 m with cost_scaling_factor 10.0 on both. Goal tolerances: xy 0.10 m, yaw 0.20 rad (general) and 3.15 rad for the goal checker that deliberately does not check heading.
why: 1 cm resolution is far finer than Nav2's usual 5 cm default and is appropriate here — a 1.2 m arena at 5 cm is only 24 cells across. robot_radius 0.15 circumscribes the 240 x 180 mm chassis. yaw_goal_tolerance > pi is the documented way to say 'heading is not checked at all' for waypoints where only position matters.

claim: Nav2 cannot localise without a laser scan IN ROS. The blocking chain is LiDAR->ROS -> TF tree -> map -> AMCL -> costmaps -> behaviour tree. Each link is useless without the one before it. Build in that order and verify each with ros2 topic echo / tf2_echo before moving on.
why: The board's /scan is dead (all ranges 0.0) and the real LiDAR belongs to fpms-rover-agent, which publishes to MQTT only. Any external Nav2 guide assumes link 1 already exists; here it had to be built (fpms_lidar_ros.py).

claim: The drive board's /scan topic is DEAD — every range is 0.0. It is not a usable LiDAR source. The real LiDAR is a D500/LD-series on its own USB path at 230400 baud, owned by fpms-rover-agent.
why: Use a topic name that does not collide with the board's dead /scan — the project publishes /scan_lidar. A subscriber that finds /scan and sees zeros will read them as obstacles at the sensor origin (LID-003).

claim: fpms_lidar_ros.py measured on this rover: publish rate 1.90 Hz at FPMS_LIDAR_HZ=2 and 9.83 Hz at 10, ~5060 raw points/s either way; MQTT round-trip latency median 100 ms, p90 179 ms. FPMS_LIDAR_HZ=10 is written to /etc/fpms/config.env on the Pi.
why: These are real measurements, not estimates, and they set the achievable costmap update rate. The 100 ms median RTT is the cost of the MQTT hop and is why LID-005 (moving the broker onto the Pi) matters.

claim: When publishing LaserScan, zero ranges must be encoded as inf or nan (LaserScan's 'no return'), NOT 0.0. Nav2 reads 0.0 as an obstacle at the sensor origin.
why: A naive MQTT-to-LaserScan bridge that passes zeros through surrounds the rover with a phantom obstacle ring centred on itself, and Nav2 will refuse to move or plan absurd escapes. This is the single most common way to get link 1 of NAV-007 subtly wrong.

claim: If the LiDAR feed goes quiet, fpms_lidar_ros.py STOPS PUBLISHING rather than repeating the last scan. A frozen scan is worse than an absent one.
why: Nav2 keeps planning against a world nobody is observing any more. Same principle as CRD-008. Also: the bridge goes through MQTT rather than the serial port on purpose — taking the port would kill the dashboard LiDAR view, and adding rclpy to fpms-rover-agent would destroy the no-ROS-dependency property that makes that agent reliable.

claim: The LiDAR takes a round trip Pi -> laptop broker -> Pi purely because the MQTT broker is off-board. Running mosquitto ON the Pi removes WiFi from a Nav2-critical path and needs NO code change, only a broker address.
why: Highest ratio of reliability gained to work done in the whole project: it deletes the WiFi dependency (OPS-002) from the scan path that Nav2's costmaps depend on, and cuts the 100 ms median RTT of LID-002.

claim: Missions default to the deadreckon backend, not nav2. deadreckon = turn-then-drive segments, closed loop on /odom pose and integrated gyro Z, with a RETRACE return; no ROS navigation stack, no map, no AMCL, no costmaps. It is the default because it is the only one of the two that has ever worked on this rover.
why: The prior autonomy (/home/ubuntu/fpms_phase6_LATEST.py) drove exactly this way and logged 0.6% distance error and +/-1-4 degrees per turn with dead reckoning as its ONLY localisation. Nav2 is worth having and is configured, but a Nav2 planning against unmeasured transforms (CRD-006) fails in ways that are genuinely hard to debug. Ship the proven path first, keep Nav2 selectable, label it honestly.

claim: backend: 'nav2' is expected to REFUSE with a specific reason until the NAV-007 chain is built. That refusal is a feature: it names the missing link instead of driving against a pose nobody has verified.
why: Matches the project-wide norm that a refusal is worth more than a plausible guess. Same shape as the mission refusing to start when the obstacle guard is blind (OPS-002).

claim: The RETRACE return is the valuable part. It does not re-plan: it replays the MEASURED outbound motions in reverse order with signs flipped (outbound turn +44.7 deg / drive +302 mm becomes return drive -302 mm / turn -44.7 deg). Every motion is undone by the number that was actually measured, not the number requested.
why: A turn that came out 2 degrees short is undone 2 degrees short, so the two errors cancel BY CONSTRUCTION rather than accumulating. This is why 'come back perfectly' worked with no SLAM, AMCL or Nav2 — and it is the strongest argument against any external source recommending re-planned returns. The return also drives BACKWARDS along the outbound path rather than turning around: two 180-degree turns are two more chances to be wrong, and undoing the outbound turns in reverse leaves the rover already facing the start heading on arrival.

claim: Terminology: a LEG is the drive to ONE target (MAX_SEGMENTS and the hold are per LEG); a SEGMENT is one commanded motion — a turn, or one bounded straight run, cut by split_legs. ROUTES chain single-target missions into one run and accumulate every measured motion into a SINGLE list unwound once.
why: A route is not three missions in a row: three missions would each retrace home and set off again — four arena crossings instead of two, and three separate chances for the re-face to be wrong. Legs are named by their single-target mission id so a route and its missions can never disagree about where a target is.

claim: Tuned constants from the prior working autonomy worth reusing by name: drive power 26, turn power 50, 20 Hz control loop, heading P-gain 10 (clamped +/-6), turn coast factor 0.93, front stop 120 mm.
why: These were tuned on THIS chassis in THIS arena and produced the 0.6% / +/-1-4 degree result. Mine the prior code rather than reinventing. Caveat: they commanded RAW DUTY, which is why its pulse widths (0.075-0.17 s) do not transfer to the velocity-setpoint path (FW-003).

claim: The dashboard arena map is WORLD-FIXED: it never rotates. Only the rover glyph moves and rotates within it, about its own centre inside a save()/restore() pair. Do not change that.
why: This is a bird's-eye POSE map, not a rover-centric radar sweep. No transform in the frontend takes rover heading and applies it to the scene. The corollary is that 'which way is forward' must be STATED, not inferred from a spinning picture — FORWARD_HEADING_DEG is that statement and the static layer paints a matching FORWARD marker at the top edge. This contradicts the common external pattern of heading-up robot maps.

claim: THE ZONE NAMING TRAP: two numbering schemes disagree. The code calls the top-LEFT zone m1 and top-RIGHT m2; the operator calls the zone directly in front of the start box 'Zone 1'. The start box is bottom-RIGHT facing 90 degrees, so the operator's 'Zone 1' is the code's m2, not m1. The fix is that NO LABEL ON THE MAP IS EVER A BARE NUMBER — every region carries the physical corner it occupies.
why: Renaming one scheme to match the other just moves the confusion. The corner is the one description the operator standing at the arena and the code running the mission cannot disagree about. ZONE_AHEAD_OF_START is DERIVED from geometry rather than typed in, so the map cannot claim a relationship the coordinates do not support.

claim: A MISSING NUMBER IS NOT ZERO. Every mission telemetry field is typed number | null. The rover OMITS fields it does not have — fpms_missions.snapshot() deliberately drops x_mm/y_mm rather than sending 0,0 — so a consumer that coerces gets a confident lie about where the rover is.
why: Pose is not published by the fleet at all: the rover renders at the assumed start pose with a POSE: SIMULATED badge. An unguarded .toFixed() on a missing pose field once WHITED OUT THE ENTIRE DASHBOARD. Field names in mission.ts are read off the real publisher, not guessed.

claim: AN UNKNOWN PHASE COUNTS AS RUNNING. `running` is false only for phases positively recognised as not-driving. A phase never heard of — new on the rover, a typo, a truncated payload — reads as RUNNING.
why: Showing 'idle' while the rover drives is the failure that gets someone to walk up to a moving machine; the reverse is merely untidy. This is the correct asymmetry for any mission console and should survive any external UI advice about 'clean' state handling.

claim: STALE TELEMETRY DURING A RUN IS LOUD. `blind` is the case that matters: the last thing heard was 'driving', and nothing has been heard since. Mission staleness threshold is deliberately SHORTER than the Drive page's TELEMETRY_STALE_MS.
why: 'The progress bar is six seconds out of date' is a materially different situation from a health panel being six seconds old. The executor throttles idle telemetry (IDLE_TELEM_S), so an IDLE mission legitimately goes quiet — which is why staleness is only loud during a run.

claim: Mission state lives in ONE place (lib/mission.ts), not inside a page component. It previously lived in Drive.tsx, which meant the mission was visible on exactly one tab: an operator watching the LiDAR map had no way to know a mission was running, and the Control tab would happily offer test_motors mid-run.
why: Every consumer inherits the hard-won rules (UI-003/004/005) by construction rather than by remembering to reimplement them. This is the structural reason the safety rules hold across tabs.

claim: NEVER restart micro-ros-agent. It costs a 90-225 s board reconnect. The board self-reconnects after an agent restart — no reset press needed. Only if genuinely wedged (no session after ~5 min) is a physical reset required.
why: Hours were lost to this. deploy_rover.py explicitly REFUSES to restart it. The retracted belief 'the board needs a reset press after every agent restart' is false.

claim: WiFi RSSI swung -47 to -78 dBm. Below about -70 the LiDAR telemetry stops crossing entirely (small drive/mission messages still get through), and the mission then refuses to start because its obstacle guard is blind. That refusal is CORRECT — move the rover nearer the host.
why: A partial-failure mode that looks like a software fault: control still works while perception silently does not. Also note fpms-wifi-powersave-hold exists because the bcmdhd driver silently re-enables WiFi power-save every 30-60 s, which flapped MQTT on a 47 s cycle.

claim: Drivetrain symmetry test: command straight, measure ODOMETRY YAW DRIFT. Reference points measured on this rover: -62 deg = one side dead, -3 deg = all four healthy, +217 deg = other side dead. A symmetric drivetrain holds heading; a weak side arcs. Then: move a known-good motor into the suspect port, move the suspect motor into a known-good port, swap only the cable.
why: A single dead rear-left lead caused a whole session's worth of phantom bugs — one side dragged, the rover pivoted, and at 50% duty that pivot threw three wheels off. It was never the mission code, CMD_SCALE, Nav2 or the firmware. This is a real automated test needing no human watching, and it is the cheapest first step.

claim: The yaw symmetry test (OPS-003) is only valid while the wiring is STILL. Motor and encoder share one connector, so moving a plug moves its encoder and the firmware's 4-wheel kinematics computes garbage heading — single pulses read -325 deg, +260 deg. Two wrong conclusions were published from that noise, including 'the M2 output stage is dead', which was false.
why: When the operator's eyes and this metric disagree mid-rewire, THE EYES WIN. A metric has a validity domain and using it outside that domain produces confident nonsense.

claim: MOTOR LAYOUT CHANGED 2026-08-01 — turn directions are MIRRORED. Now M1=FRONT-RIGHT, M2=REAR-RIGHT, M3=FRONT-LEFT, M4=REAR-LEFT (previously M1 front-left, M2 rear-left, M3 front-right, M4 rear-right). Firmware treats M1/M2 as one side and M3/M4 as the other, so FORWARD is unaffected but every TURN is mirrored versus what the mission code assumes.
why: Verify turn sign before trusting any heading control. NOTE: NAV2_BRIEF.md section 2 still documents the OLD layout — SESSION_HANDOFF.md is dated 2026-08-01 and supersedes it. This is an unreconciled contradiction between two project files and the newer one wins.

claim: Both CP2102 adapters report an IDENTICAL ID_SERIAL. Only the USB topology path distinguishes them. NEVER bind by /dev/ttyUSBn — enumeration order is not guaranteed. Drive board: platform-fc880000.usb-usb-0:1.3:1.0-port0 @ 921600. LiDAR: ...-usb-0:1.2:1.0-port0 @ 230400.
why: Getting it wrong sends motor commands to the LiDAR.

claim: ROS_DOMAIN_ID = 20 is MANDATORY on every ROS call; the firmware stores this itself. Every ros2 command silently returns NOTHING USEFUL — not an error, just no output — if it is wrong.
why: A silent-empty failure mode is indistinguishable from 'the topic is dead', which is exactly the diagnosis this project has twice wasted hours on. Export it in every shell alongside sourcing /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash.

claim: The board went silent ~15 min after a reset, twice — then ran over an hour once the drivetrain was fixed. Suspect current draw from the dragging motor, not a timer. If topics die, CHECK BOARD LIVENESS FIRST.
why: Every downstream symptom of a dead board looks like a software fault: blind executor, frozen poses, probes returning zero. Battery was ~12.2 V and fell to 11.4 V during a long session. Battery topic is UInt16 in DECIVOLTS (divide by 10).

claim: Only ONE agent touches the Pi at a time. Concurrent SSH has already caused a protocol-banner failure and a corrupted measurement run. Never publish /cmd_vel unless the task explicitly authorises motion, and then only bounded, short, with a zero Twist after.
why: Both rules exist because they were broken and cost real time. The /cmd_vel rule is doubly important given FW-002: there is no gentle duty, so an accidental publish is never a gentle mistake.

claim: The board answers its CONFIG protocol (115200, frames 0xFF/0xF8 out, 0xF7 back, checksum = sum % 256) only in the first ~5 s after reset. Rosmaster_Lib CANNOT talk to this board — wrong protocol, it is for the STM32 Rosmaster. It returns version=-1, battery 0.0, encoders 0.
why: Those zeros mean WRONG PROTOCOL, not dead hardware — another instance of the project's recurring 'suspect the measurement before the mechanism' pattern. Also retracted: car_type (0x05) selects the micro-ROS TRANSPORT (0=WiFi-UDP, 1=RPi5 serial, 2=RISC-V), not the chassis; it cannot invert motion.

claim: NOT VERIFIED — the rover was powered off before any of it ran end to end: whether fpms-lidar-ros is actually installed and enabled (the docstring and deploy_rover.py both SAY installed, but this was never confirmed with systemctl status while the rover was up); the Nav2 launch as a whole; any mission end to end; the deadband, which has NEVER been measured on corrected data.
why: None of this is known-broken. It is UNPROVEN, which is not the same thing, and the fastest way to waste a session is to treat it as either. deadband_sweep.py was fixed to use pose but never re-run.

claim: THE SINGLE MOST USEFUL THING TO KNOW: this project has repeatedly been derailed by confident conclusions drawn from untrustworthy measurements. Neither of the two multi-hour losses was found by tuning — both were found by a TEST DESIGNED TO DISCRIMINATE BETWEEN HYPOTHESES (comparing twist against pose for the same event; reading the firmware source). When something looks impossible, suspect the MEASUREMENT before the mechanism.
why: This is the meta-rule that generated most of the OVERRIDE records above. Corollary that also earned its keep: two agents REFUSED TO GUESS when they lacked hardware access and said so — that refusal is why the right answer was found instead of a plausible wrong one. Preserve that norm.

claim: This repo is PUBLIC. No secrets in committed files. The first draft of NAV2_BRIEF.md leaked the SSH password and had to be scrubbed before commit. The Pi password is read from the FPMS_PI_PASSWORD environment variable, never hardcoded.
why: It is an easy mistake to make while writing 'helpful' documentation — the leak happened in a file whose entire purpose was to be helpful. Worker secrets likewise use `wrangler secret put` and never land in wrangler.toml or git.

claim: Windows Mobile Hotspot turns itself off when no device is connected, which cost a 12-minute boot delay. It must be ON BEFORE the rover powers up or the Pi boots with no network and takes ~12 minutes to appear. Disable that auto-off setting.
why: Pure wall-clock waste at the start of every session, and it masquerades as 'the rover is dead'. IPv4 fallbacks seen: 192.168.137.181, .201, .73 (DHCP moves); fpms-pi.local resolves to an IPv6 link-local address so a plain connect(host) fails.

claim: There is NO driveOnHeading() in the Humble BasicNavigator. The Humble Python wrapper ships only spin() and backup(); DriveOnHeading exists as an action server and BT node but not in nav2_simple_commander. Getting it from Python on Humble means building the nav2_msgs/action/DriveOnHeading client yourself (~15 lines).
why: Verified against the Humble branch source. The two primitives this project most needs are precisely the ones with rough edges on Humble (see also R1-007). Do not assume the helper exists.

claim: Nav2's own repo ships odometry_calibration.xml — a behaviour tree whose entire purpose is driving a square from DriveOnHeading (dist_to_travel, a DISPLACEMENT terminated on measured pose delta) plus Spin (spin_dist, a yaw delta). Upstream Nav2 therefore already endorses segment-and-settle when a controller cannot be trusted.
why: R1 calls this the most applicable single artefact found, and it is: the `speed` argument being ignored-in-effect by our firmware does not matter because the TERMINATION CONDITION is what gives accuracy. This is upstream validation of the segment-and-stop architecture the project already chose for its deadreckon backend (MIS-001). Scale the numbers: dist_to_travel 2.0 -> 0.2..0.5, time_allowance 12 -> 4..6.

claim: RPP's entire value proposition is MODULATING LINEAR VELOCITY, and all five of its regulation knobs (use_regulated_linear_velocity_scaling, use_cost_regulated_linear_velocity_scaling, approach_velocity_scaling_dist, min_approach_linear_velocity, regulated_linear_scaling_min_speed) are NO-OPS on a chassis that outputs 50% duty for any non-zero setpoint. RPP will compute a beautiful 0.05 m/s approach and the rover will launch at full speed into the goal.
why: This is R1's single biggest NOT-APPLICABLE and it independently rediscovers the reasoning already written into nav2_params.yaml (NAV-004), which disabled or floored exactly these five knobs. AGREEMENT, not conflict. But see R1-004 for the deeper consequence the project's config does NOT address.

claim: DERIVED CONSEQUENCE: with every taper disabled or floored, RPP degenerates to a constant-velocity geometric path follower that still emits CONTINUOUS /cmd_vel. The firmware turns any continuous non-zero setpoint into continuous 50% duty. So the neutered RPP config does NOT produce the segment-and-stop motion that FW-005 prescribes — it produces continuous cruise.
why: This is the gap between the project's Nav2 config and its own design rule. nav2_params.yaml correctly stops RPP commanding IMPOSSIBLE speeds, but it cannot make RPP produce the STOP-BETWEEN-SEGMENTS motion model. The deadreckon backend (MIS-001) does produce it; the Nav2 backend as configured does not. R1's section 4.3 synthesis is the resolution: keep Nav2's top (mission sequencing) and bottom (Spin/DriveOnHeading primitives) and skip the middle (controller_server FollowPath).

claim: Humble cannot disable collision checks on Spin — the flag exists in newer Nav2 but is missing in Humble (upstream issue 5633). In a 1.2 m arena with walls 0.6 m away and default inflation, Spin's forward-projection collision check will frequently VETO legitimate rotations.
why: Directly blocks the turn half of turn-then-drive if Nav2's Spin is used. Either shrink inflation drastically or run a bespoke spin primitive. This is a concrete reason the project's own deadreckon turn implementation may remain the better path even after Nav2 works.

claim: The Nav2 behavior server projects the current odom TWIST forward to do collision checking (simulate_ahead_time). With /odom_raw twist sign-inverted, that projection points BACKWARDS and the behavior can abort with a phantom collision. Anything consuming odom twist — behavior server, velocity smoother, progress checker, DWB, StoppedGoalChecker — inherits the fault.
why: This is the highest-value cross-reference in R1: it connects the project's measured ODO-001 fault to a specific list of Nav2 components that will misbehave. The sign MUST be fixed in a republisher BEFORE any Nav2 node subscribes. fpms_odom_tf.py already republishes a corrected /odom — the action item is ensuring every Nav2 node reads THAT, never /odom_raw.

claim: Upstream Nav2 defaults destroy a 1.2 m arena, with arithmetic: local costmap 3x3 m is 6.25x the arena; inflation_radius 0.55 vs an arena half-width of 0.6 m leaves every cell except a ~0.1x0.1 m patch at the exact centre carrying inflated cost (no gradient to descend); robot_radius 0.22 puts a lethal band around all four walls leaving a 0.76 m free square; xy_goal_tolerance 0.25 is 21% of arena width; planner tolerance 0.5 is 42%; progress checker required_movement_radius 0.5 within 10 s will false-trigger on a burst-driven chassis.
why: The project's nav2_params.yaml already overrides most of these (NAV-006). The progress-checker point is the one worth re-checking: a segment-and-stop motion model with settle pauses is exactly the pattern SimpleProgressChecker false-triggers on. R1 recommends required_movement_radius 0.05 and movement_time_allowance 20.0.

claim: THERE IS NO PUBLISHED NAV2 PARAM SET FOR A SUB-2 M ARENA. Neither TurtleBot3 Burger (robot_radius 0.1) nor linorobot2 goes below resolution 0.05 or inflation_radius 0.5, and the Nav2 maintainers' own advice — 'increase your inflation layer cost scale and radius to adequately produce a smooth potential across the entire map' — is room-scale reasoning that INVERTS at 1.2 m.
why: You are deriving these numbers, not copying them. This is itself the finding: the project is outside the envelope every published config was tuned for, so copying wholesale fails. It also means the project's own nav2_params.yaml derivations cannot be validated against any reference — only against the bench.

claim: THE MOTION QUANTUM RULE: the minimum achievable displacement is v_full x 0.35 s. Any xy_goal_tolerance tighter than that quantum is a GUARANTEED INFINITE OSCILLATION — the rover can never land inside the tolerance band. Measure v_full first, compute the quantum, set xy_goal_tolerance >= 1.5 x quantum. R1 calls this the single most important number in its document and says it cannot be sourced from any repo, only from the bench.
why: POTENTIAL LIVE CONFLICT with nav2_params.yaml's xy_goal_tolerance of 0.10 m. SESSION_HANDOFF records '0.35 s pulse MOVES, ~0.18 per pulse' free-spinning, and FW-004 records a ~6x wire-to-real gain. If v_full under load is anywhere near 0.5 m/s the quantum is ~0.18 m — LARGER than the configured 0.10 m tolerance, which would make every Nav2 goal oscillate forever. This is DERIVED and UNVERIFIED: it depends entirely on v_full measured under load, which nobody has done. It is the cheapest high-consequence check available.

claim: To run Nav2 with no localisation: set global_frame: odom on BOTH costmaps and drop the map frame entirely (Nav2 docs: 'if your system does not have a map_frame, you can remove it and make sure world_frame is set to the value of odom_frame'). ALSO drop the static_layer from both costmaps — with no localisation a static map layer progressively disagrees with reality as drift accumulates, producing ghost walls the rover refuses to drive through. Preferred over publishing a fake static identity map->odom, which lies by asserting drift is zero.
why: CONFLICTS with the project's nav2_params.yaml, whose global_costmap includes a StaticLayer against nav2/arena_map.yaml with AMCL configured. Resolution by PHASE, not by winner: R1 is right for the INTERIM (Nav2 running before AMCL, which is today per NAV-007 and CRD-004); the project's config is right for the eventual AMCL-enabled state. Without this change every Nav2 lifecycle node stalls waiting for map->odom. Understand what it buys: the global costmap becomes a dead-reckoned frame, and ghost obstacles from drift will NOT fully raytrace-clear because the drift is in the pose, not the scan.

claim: Use StoppedGoalChecker instead of SimpleGoalChecker: it requires the robot to be STOPPED inside tolerance before declaring success, converting 'arrived' from a position test into a position-AND-stopped test — the settle half of segment-and-settle, for free. Verified Humble defaults trans_stopped_velocity and rot_stopped_velocity are BOTH 0.25, far too loose for a bang-bang chassis; tighten to ~0.02 / 0.05.
why: The project currently configures SimpleGoalChecker (NAV-006). HAZARD, and it is ours specifically: StoppedGoalChecker reads odom TWIST. Given ODO-001, magnitude is presumably still correct so the stopped test likely works — but VERIFY, because if the driver reports a stale non-zero twist after a burst ends, the goal checker will never fire and the mission hangs forever.

claim: Raise waypoint_pause_duration aggressively from the upstream 200 ms default to 1500-3000 ms, and set stop_on_failure: true. The pause is FREE ACCURACY: it lets the chassis fully stop, lets the ~9.8 Hz LiDAR deliver 15-30 clean stationary scans, and lets IMU yaw settle before the next leg's heading is computed.
why: Directly enables both the gyro bias re-estimation (FUS-003) and the stop-and-fix LiDAR correction (R2-012), which both need stationary windows. stop_on_failure matters because in a 1.2 m arena, silently skipping a failed waypoint means the rover is somewhere unknown.

claim: nav2_velocity_smoother has a deadband_velocity parameter documented as 'minimum thresholds, below which we set its value to 0 ... useful when your robot's breaking torque from stand still is non-trivial so sending very small values will pull high amounts of current'. It is the right idea for the OPPOSITE problem and cannot create a slow speed.
why: Worth setting as a DON'T-TWITCH FILTER, not as a speed controller: it zeroes Nav2's regulated trickle-speeds rather than letting the firmware turn each one into a full-speed lurch. Note this is the mechanism whose absence NAV2_BRIEF retracted as the phantom 'MIN_CMD floor' (both project floors are now 0.0 and marked unmeasured) — so re-introducing it needs the real measured floor first, not a guess.

claim: How do real projects handle a chassis that cannot creep? THEY DON'T HAVE THIS PROBLEM, BECAUSE THEY FIX IT IN FIRMWARE. The universal ROS-community solution is a minimum-PWM map plus feedforward deadband compensation: find the PWM at which wheels just begin to turn under load, map commanded velocity onto [PWM_min, PWM_max] rather than [0, PWM_max], and close a PI loop on encoder feedback. The measured symptom (0.0010 fast, 0.00295 dead, load-dependent) is the textbook signature of no PWM mapping and no closed-loop speed control on the ESP32.
why: THE FORK IN THE ROAD. If the ESP32 is in scope, this deletes the cannot-creep constraint entirely and unlocks RPP, DWB, MPPI and the whole Nav2 controller stack. If the ESP32 is OUT of scope, then every continuous-velocity controller in Nav2 is permanently NOT APPLICABLE and the burst-primitive architecture is not a workaround — IT IS THE CORRECT ARCHITECTURE. This agrees with NAV2_BRIEF section 3b's own conclusion that the real fix is the encoder/wheel constants, i.e. a firmware rebuild.

claim: Stop-and-fix against known walls: the arena is a known 1.2 x 1.2 m rectangle and there is a 2D LiDAR, so while stopped at a segment boundary you can fit lines to the walls and recover absolute (x, y, yaw) — no AMCL, no SLAM, no particle filter. Two perpendicular walls fully determine planar pose in a known rectangle. R1 rates this the best fit to this hardware of anything in the report and its #1 recommendation.
why: STRONG CONVERGENCE: R1 and R2 independently arrived at this as their top recommendation, and the project has ALREADY IMPLEMENTED THE MATHS (see R2-008 and the wall_fit/manhattan_offset/arena_fix_from_scan functions in fpms_odom_tf.py). It exploits every constraint rather than fighting them: 9.8 Hz is plenty when stopped, it needs no continuous motion, and it converts unbounded drift into bounded per-leg error. Three independent sources agreeing is the strongest signal in this knowledge base.

claim: NEGATIVE RESULT: no public repo was found doing plan-then-follow in a sub-2 m arena with a bang-bang chassis and no localisation. Closest architectural match is AntonioConsiglio/rover_ros2 (Pi 5 + ESP32 micro-ROS + Humble + Nav2, repo fetched and confirmed) but it exposes no Nav2 param files or waypoint code. linorobot2 and TurtleBot3 params were fetched and verified; RoverRobotics, Rosmo, albertrichard080 and forg_bot are existence-only from the search index and their contents were NOT verified.
why: Honest scoping of what the survey did and did not establish. The absence is itself informative (see R1-008). Do not cite the existence-only repos for specifics — R1 explicitly marks them unverified.

claim: R1's recommended synthesis: USE NAV2, BUT ONLY THE TOP AND BOTTOM — SKIP THE MIDDLE. KEEP nav2_simple_commander / BT navigator for mission sequencing, nav2_behaviors (Spin, DriveOnHeading) for primitives, nav2_waypoint_follower with a long pause, StoppedGoalChecker, and costmaps only for obstacle checking. SKIP controller_server FollowPath with RPP/DWB, AMCL, map_server/static_layer, and velocity smoothing that assumes a continuous actuator. ADD the LiDAR wall-fix corrector, the twist-sign republisher, and the burst sequencer.
why: This satisfies the operator's Nav2 requirement and keeps the migration path open (if the ESP32 is ever fixed per R1-014, the full controller stack becomes usable WITHOUT rewriting the mission layer) while putting accuracy where it actually comes from. R1 argues the case against Nav2 even-handedly first: it is architecturally a drift-correction CONSUMER, not a drift-tolerant system, and with ~10 lifecycle nodes between goal and wheels, 'the rover went 8 cm too far' becomes a multi-hour investigation that a 200-line sequencer makes a one-minute read.

claim: waitUntilNav2Active(navigator='bt_navigator', localizer='amcl') will HANG FOREVER waiting for a lifecycle node that does not exist when there is no AMCL. Call it as waitUntilNav2Active(localizer=None).
why: A one-argument fix for a symptom (Nav2 bringup appears to start then silently never becomes ready) that would otherwise read as a broken launch file. Directly relevant because the project runs without AMCL today.

claim: REP-105: a localisation fix computes map->base_link, but must publish map->odom = (map->base_link)_fix * inverse((odom->base_link)_odometry). It must NEVER rewrite odom->base_link, because a frame may have only one parent and because odom is contractually SMOOTH ('always evolves in a smooth way, without discrete jumps') while map explicitly MAY jump ('can change in discrete jumps at any time').
why: Controllers, local costmaps and velocity estimators differentiate odom and will produce a fake velocity spike if it is teleported. Discrete map jumps are EXPECTED and FINE — that is exactly where a LiDAR fix belongs. GOOD NEWS: the project's existing (disabled) fix path is already named map_to_odom_from_fix, i.e. the design is already REP-105-correct; the map edge is simply absent because LIDAR_FIX_ENABLED is False.

claim: On a skid-steer the wheels must scrub laterally, so the vehicle rotates about an instantaneous centre of rotation displaced from the geometric axle. The EFFECTIVE track that makes encoder-derived yaw correct is LARGER than the geometric track, commonly by roughly 1.5-2.5x, and it is NOT CONSTANT — it varies with surface friction, load, tyre wear and turn rate.
why: INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMS the project's FUS-004 decision. TRACK_M = 0.170 is the geometric track and would be badly wrong as an effective track — but the project never uses it for heading. Using the gyro sidesteps the single largest systematic error on a skid-steer chassis FOR FREE. R2 states explicitly this 'should be preserved, not fixed by switching to encoder-derived yaw'.

claim: UMBmark's two corrections are BOTH INAPPLICABLE to this rover. Ed (wheel-diameter ratio) needs per-wheel control to apply, and there is no per-wheel encoder topic and no /joint_states — we cannot observe or apply a left/right split. Eb (effective-wheelbase) calibrates encoder-derived yaw, WHICH WE DO NOT USE. What IS applicable is the straight-line SCALE calibration: the single scalar mapping /odom_raw pose-delta to true ground distance.
why: DIRECT CONFLICT WITH R1's top-5 item #5, which recommends running the full bidirectional UMBmark. R2 WINS: its reasoning is specific to our sensor set and was verified against the code (no /joint_states publisher; heading integrated from gyro at fpms_odom_tf.py:1689). Nuance worth keeping: the project's own M2 asks for the skid-steer effective-track factor via a four-90-degree-turn pattern — but as a WITNESS that quantifies the heading-source argument, explicitly 'turns nothing on', not as a correction to apply.

claim: STRAIGHT-LINE SCALE CALIBRATION is the single highest-value calibration available to this rover and it is a 20-minute bench job: drive a measured 1000 mm, read the integrated distance, correct MM_PER_TICK / WHEEL_DIAMETER_M (fpms_odom_tf.py:368-373) by the ratio, forward and backward, 5x each, averaged. Expected: a typical 1-3% unmodelled distance-scale error drops to roughly 0.2-0.5%, i.e. from 10-30 mm/m down to 2-5 mm/m.
why: The current constants (WHEEL_DIAMETER_M 0.070, TICKS_PER_REV 1320, MM_PER_TICK 0.16657) are nominal and unverified — and FW-004 records that the fitted hardware demonstrably does NOT match the firmware's constants (a ~6x discrepancy). Read the budget honestly though: R2 notes this attacks only the THIRD-largest error term; the assumed start pose and accumulated heading dominate and are unobservable proprioceptively.

claim: A robot_localization EKF here is a SMOOTHING AND PLUMBING win, not an accuracy win: better-conditioned velocity estimates, proper covariance propagation, a standards-compliant odom->base_link publisher. It CANNOT reduce unbounded drift because every input is proprioceptive. Expect 0 mm of improvement in absolute arena position. robot_localization is installed but no EKF config exists anywhere in the repo.
why: CRITICAL BLOCKER, ours specifically: the documented best practice is FUSE THE TWIST, NOT THE POSE ('if the odometry provides both position and linear velocity, fuse the linear velocity'). Our twist is sign-inverted (ODO-001), so feeding /odom_raw straight into odom0 with vx: true would make the EKF integrate motion BACKWARDS. Any EKF adoption must be fed a sign-corrected republished topic. Useful config rules: two_d_mode: true for a planar robot; never inflate covariances to suppress a variable (disable it in the config matrix instead); tune process noise only after measurement covariances are honest.

claim: DERIVED wall-fit accuracy for this arena: ~±3-5 mm in x/y and ~±0.15-0.3 deg in yaw from a single scan. Chain: LD06 single-shot range accuracy ~±15 mm at 1 deg resolution; all four walls visible from everywhere in a 1200 mm arena so (x,y,yaw) is FULLY OBSERVABLE from one scan; a wall at ~600 mm spans ~90 deg i.e. ~90 points; line fitting reduces the random perpendicular component by sqrt(N) giving 15/sqrt(90) ~ 1.6 mm; angle error ~15*sqrt(12/90)/1200 rad ~ 0.26 deg per wall, halved to ~0.13 deg by averaging four orthogonal walls.
why: This is the quantitative case that ±1 cm is achievable at all. A structural bonus of a CLOSED rectangle: systematic range bias does not average down, but it largely CANCELS IN POSITION — a uniform +b mm bias pushes all four walls outward symmetrically, perturbing the inferred arena SIZE rather than the CENTRE. The project's wall_fit() already returns span_error_m, which measures exactly that bias for free on every fix.

claim: A SQUARE arena is 90-degree rotationally symmetric, so a Manhattan-frame estimate is only ever YAW MODULO 90 DEGREES. With 1200x1200 there is no geometric way to break the tie from a single scan — not even wall-length matching. The quadrant MUST be disambiguated by the gyro/odometry prior. Mitigation: gate every fix against the gyro prior and REJECT any fix implying a >45 degree correction, logging it loudly rather than applying it.
why: A silent, catastrophic failure mode specific to this arena's squareness. It compounds with R2-008: a mirrored scan of a square arena also fits perfectly. Both failures produce a CONFIDENT WRONG pose rather than an error.

claim: AMCL IS THE WRONG TOOL FOR A ±1 CM TARGET. Published AMCL translational RMSE is ~8.5 cm in an empty environment, degrading to ~33.7 cm in a cluttered office — 10-30x short. AMCL is designed for large, cluttered, ambiguous environments where the hard problem is GLOBAL ambiguity; our problem is the opposite (exact, tiny, fully observable map). A direct wall-fit / point-to-line ICP is both simpler and roughly 10x more accurate here, because it does not quantise the world into a grid and does not represent the posterior with a finite particle set.
why: AGREES with R1's recommendation to skip AMCL. The project already configures AMCL in nav2_params.yaml against nav2/arena_map.yaml but has never launched it — keep it as a Nav2-compatible fallback for robustness, do not rely on it for precision.

claim: DEAD RECKONING ALONE CANNOT DELIVER ±1 CM ABSOLUTE ARENA POSITION — not over 1 m, not with any tuning, not in principle. Three independent reasons: (1) the START POSE IS ASSUMED, not measured — hand placement to ±15 mm and ±3 deg is already outside a ±10 mm budget before the rover moves, and 3 deg of heading error alone contributes 1000*sin(3deg) = 52 mm of lateral error over a 1 m leg; (2) error is UNBOUNDED BY CONSTRUCTION per REP-105; (3) skid-steer slip is NON-SYSTEMATIC and is precisely the class calibration cannot remove. Budget: ~±40-75 mm RSS per leg, 50-150 mm+ absolute after several legs.
why: Sets honest expectations against the project's own measured 0.6% distance error (FUS-002). NO CONTRADICTION between the two: 0.6% is RELATIVE distance error along a leg, whereas R2 is describing ABSOLUTE arena position including the unobservable start-pose terms. Both are true and they measure different things. The retrace strategy (MIS-003) is precisely what makes the relative number good without needing the absolute one.

claim: WITH the LiDAR arena fix enabled and stop-and-fix at each waypoint, the RSS budget at a fix point is ~±5-9 mm, and ~±10-15 mm mid-leg between fixes. ±1 cm is achievable AT FIX POINTS, AND ONLY AT FIX POINTS. The dominant remaining term is the LiDAR mount-yaw calibration residual (±3-5 mm at 0.5 deg over a 600 mm lever arm).
why: This is the target to design missions around: place fix points where accuracy actually matters (dock/hold positions) rather than expecting continuous centimetre accuracy. If ±1 cm were required CONTINUOUSLY, fixes would have to be taken in motion with proper timestamping and the 9.83 Hz MQTT-transported scan rate becomes the binding constraint.

claim: LIDAR MOUNT YAW IS THE DOMINANT ERROR TERM and must be calibrated to < 0.5 deg. A constant mount-yaw error d rotates the entire inferred pose about the sensor; across a 600 mm arena half-width that is 600*d of position error, so 1 DEGREE OF UNCALIBRATED MOUNT YAW = ~10.5 MM — on its own that blows the entire ±1 cm budget. Separately, LIDAR_ROTATION_SIGN being wrong MIRRORS the scan, which in a SQUARE arena produces a plausible-looking but wrong fit: a silent failure mode.
why: Both LIDAR_ZERO_OFFSET_DEG (0.0) and LIDAR_ROTATION_SIGN (-1) are marked UNVERIFIED in fpms_lidar_ros.py:164-168, and LASER_YAW_RAD in nav2/fpms_tf.launch.py is a placeholder (CRD-006). Verified present in the code. The project quantifies the mirror hazard further than R2 does — see PROJECT-M5 record OPS-015.

claim: TAKE FIXES AT REST — the decisive design choice. The scan arrives at ~9.83 Hz over MQTT, so its true age is one scan period plus broker transport (~105 ms + transport); at 0.15 m/s that is >=16 mm of travel, larger than the entire error budget. Stopping between legs, taking 3-5 scans and fitting while stationary drives the latency error to ZERO, buys a further sqrt(5) on the random term, and makes the discrete map jump happen exactly when REP-105 says it is safe.
why: ALREADY IMPLEMENTED as project policy: LIDAR_FIX_REQUIRE_STILL = True in fpms_odom_tf.py, whose own comment notes that at the mission TURN RATE of 0.45 rad/s the same latency is up to 4.6 degrees of heading — larger than the whole error the fix is trying to remove — and that fpms_missions.py already stops between every segment so this costs nothing. The project's reasoning is sharper than R2's (it identifies rotation, not translation, as the binding term).

claim: PHYSICALLY MEASURE THE ARENA. ARENA_MM = 1200.0 is a DESIGN value replicated in three files (fpms_odom_tf.py:589, fpms_missions.py:277, nav2/make_arena_map.py:103, plus frontend/src/lib/arena.ts as the source of truth). If the real box is 1204 x 1197 mm, that error goes straight into every wall fix (±2-5 mm in the budget).
why: A tape measure removes a term that no amount of algorithm work can. Note the arena is treated as SQUARE throughout, which is also what makes the Manhattan quadrant ambiguity (R2-007) unbreakable — if the real box turns out to be rectangular, that ambiguity becomes breakable geometrically.

claim: SEED THE INITIAL POSE FROM A LIDAR FIX instead of assuming it. This directly deletes rows 1 and 2 of the dead-reckoning budget — the assumed start position (±10-20 mm) and assumed start heading (±30-50 mm) — which are the two largest terms, for essentially no cost once the wall fit works.
why: Also removes the recurring operational hazard behind ODO-006 (a stale origin once put the rover at (-9182, -11926) mm in a 1200 mm arena). A measured start pose is both more accurate and more robust than a re-zeroing ritual that a human must remember after every boot.

claim: PROJECT OVERRIDE ON THE LIDAR FIX. fpms_odom_tf.py:576-583 states LIDAR_FIX_ENABLED 'is not a convenience switch. Turning it on without M4, M5 and M6 from the docstring produces a pose correction that is CONFIDENT and WRONG, which is strictly worse than the dead reckoning it would replace, because dead-reckoning error is smooth and recognisable while a bad absolute fix teleports the robot.' lidar_fix_blockers() enumerates what is missing and the node refuses with those reasons at startup. The gating measurements are M4 (LiDAR mount transform, above all LASER_YAW_RAD in nav2/fpms_tf.launch.py), M5 (LIDAR_ZERO_OFFSET_DEG and LIDAR_ROTATION_SIGN), and M6 (do PHYSICAL WALLS exist at the scanner's mounting height?).
why: OVERRIDES R2's recommendation #1 to 'flip LIDAR_FIX_ENABLED — highest value by a wide margin — the code is already written and tested'. R2 is RIGHT about the priority and WRONG about the method: the flag is the LAST step, not the first. R2 also entirely MISSED M6 — if the 1200x1200 boundary is tape on the floor, or the wall is shorter than the LiDAR is tall, there is nothing to fit and the whole correction design is VOID. Nobody has recorded this either way, and it is a five-second observation that gates every other item in the accuracy programme.

claim: THE MIRROR BLIND SPOT, QUANTIFIED. A wrong LIDAR_ROTATION_SIGN mirrors the scan, and a mirrored scan of a SQUARE arena still fits a square perfectly, so wall_fit returns a confident, wrong, REFLECTED pose. The reflection is about the arena centre line, so the error is 2*|coord - 600 mm| — meaning the sanity check against dead reckoning only catches it beyond LIDAR_MAX_JUMP_M, and WITHIN 150 MM OF THE CENTRE LINE A MIRRORED SCAN IS ACCEPTED WITH UP TO 300 MM OF ERROR AND NO COMPLAINT. --selftest demonstrates this rather than asserting it.
why: The project calls this 'the single most dangerous unmeasured item on the list because it is the one that fails silently'. It sharpens R2-011's general warning into an exact blind-spot geometry. This is why M5 must be verified by the documented wall test before the fix is trusted, not inferred from a fit that looks plausible.

claim: Our map is permanently Foxglove Follow = OFF with fixed frame = arena, equivalently RViz Fixed Frame = map rather than base_link. Rover-centric views are correct for SENSOR DEBUGGING (is the scan aligned to the chassis?) and wrong for SPATIAL REASONING (where is that obstacle in the arena?). The corollary the reference tools also teach: because the view never rotates, FORWARD must be STATED on the map.
why: INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMS the project's UI-001 world-fixed decision and supplies the industry vocabulary for it. R3 audited the existing ArenaMap.tsx and found seven properties it already gets right that reference tools get WRONG by default — including the single ctx.rotate() inside drawRover's save/restore, the trail lifting the pen on TRAIL_BREAK rather than joining across resets (better than Mission Planner), and absent values rendering '--' never '0' (matching MAVLink's explicit unknown sentinels). These must not be regressed.

claim: DEFECT 1 (VERIFIED IN CODE): THEME_DARK.assumed and CLASS_COLORS_DARK[3] are the SAME HEX '#fbbf24'; identically in light mode assumed === '#b45309' === CLASS_COLORS_LIGHT[3]. So the amber ghost rover, the amber assumed trail and every OBSTACLE LiDAR point are one colour — the provenance channel and a sensor-data channel are literally indistinguishable.
why: VERIFIED directly: ArenaMap.tsx defines assumed/trailAssumed as '#fbbf24' and lidarCluster.ts defines CLASS_COLORS_DARK as ['#475569','#94a3b8','#4ade80','#fbbf24']. The one channel that must never be misread — is this pose real? — shares a colour with ordinary sensor data. Amber should be reserved for provenance (a STATUS, not a series); re-hue the OBSTACLE class.

claim: DEFECT 2 IS STALE — DO NOT ACT ON IT. R3 reports a three-way blue collision with trailMeasured at '#38bdf8' measuring dE 6.7 against the water station '#22d3ee'. The current code has ALREADY FIXED THIS: THEME_DARK.trailMeasured is '#34d399' (emerald) and THEME_LIGHT.trailMeasured is '#047857', with an in-code comment documenting the change and its own validation (dark dE 15.7 normal / 12.7 deutan; light dE 28.6 / 23.9).
why: R3 audited a palette one revision behind the working tree. The remaining question is only the TWO-way pair of planned-route sky ('#7dd3fc') against water-station cyan ('#22d3ee'), which is a real but much smaller issue than reported. This record exists so a later agent does not 'fix' a defect that is already fixed and regress a validated colour choice. Defects 1 and 3 were checked against current code and DO still stand.

claim: DEFECT 3 (STANDS): measured-emerald '#34d399' and danger-rose '#fb7185' measure dE 4.6 deutan / 3.0 tritan — POSE MEASURED and LINK DOWN / near-obstacle danger are the same colour to a deuteranope. Swapping to other red/green steps does not fix it ('#0ca30c' vs '#d03b3b' measures dE 4.1 deutan); red/green never will. The rule is that status colours ship with an ICON + LABEL, never colour alone.
why: The HUD badge already carries text so it is mitigated THERE, but the < 150 mm danger RING is encoded in hue alone and is not. That ring is the safety-critical state the obstacle guard acts on. Add a second ring, a '!' glyph, or a 'NEAR 120mm' label.

claim: ABORT MUST ALWAYS BE RENDERED, IN A FIXED POSITION. MissionStrip.tsx renders ABORT MISSION only when (running || f.blind) — verified at MissionStrip.tsx:189 — so the button's presence and position change with state, which destroys the muscle memory that makes an abort fast. ISO 13850 requires an E-stop actuator to be 'readily accessible', which is a LAYOUT requirement, not a wording one. Always render it; disable it only when there is provably nothing to stop, and even then keep the footprint.
why: VERIFIED in code. Add a global keyboard shortcut and KEEP the existing 'ungated by link checks' rule — R3 explicitly says that code comment is correct and should be preserved verbatim. Related: R3 recommends stating whether ABORT is a recoverable stop or a latching one and what the recovery path is (PX4 distinguishes Kill, revertible within 5 s, from Flight Termination, not revertible without reboot).

claim: Replace the pulsing uncertainty halo with a MODELLED DRIFT RING whose radius grows with driven distance and accumulated turn: r = k_d * sum|ds| + k_theta * sum|dpsi| * L, labelled 'DRIFT >= ±NN cm (modelled, unmeasured)'. RViz draws covariance at a stated sigma in world units precisely because an uncertainty with a SIZE can be compared to the arena; an animation-driven radius is a DECORATIVE magnitude that reads as a radar ping and invites the eye to ignore it.
why: Two supporting reasons. First, prefers-reduced-motion CANNOT reach the halo: index.css disables CSS animation globally but the halo is drawn by drawRover inside the rAF loop, so no CSS rule touches it — read the media query once in the effect, store it in a ref, and render a STATIC ring. Second, the project already tracks both inputs (PoseTrail gives cumulative distance, heading integration gives accumulated yaw), so this is a declared model rather than a measurement, and it is more honest than a fixed or pulsing circle because it visibly grows the longer the rover drives without a fix.

claim: SHOW POSE AGE INLINE, copying Foxglove's idiom verbatim: render the pose readout muted with the age inline, 'X 620 mm (4.2s ago)'. Then copy RViz's TF Frame Timeout behaviour: GREY THE GLYPH PROGRESSIVELY over the last third of a timeout window, then STOP DRAWING IT and leave only the caption. Pose arrives on a 0.2 Hz heartbeat against a 2 Hz scan, so the glyph can be five seconds stale while the cloud looks live.
why: Extends the project's own UI-005 staleness principle to the map layer, and the graduated-decay-then-absence pattern matches LID-004's rule that a faint picture is still a picture. RViz's concrete precedent is Frame Timeout 15 s with fade over the last 1/3. R3 explicitly says KEEP the existing HUD wording (POSE ASSUMED / NOTHING REPORTED A POSITION / DEAD-RECKONED - NOT LOCALISED) — it is a class stated in words, exactly QGC's fix_type pattern and better than most commercial consoles. Add age and radius; change nothing about the phrasing.

claim: DRAG-TO-RE-ZERO — R3's highest-leverage addition. Freedom Robotics makes relocalisation DIRECT MANIPULATION: drag the inner circle to translate, the semi-transparent outer ring to rotate, WITH THE LIVE LIDAR OVERLAID AS THE ALIGNMENT CUE, publishing PoseWithCovarianceStamped to /initialpose. We have the same preconditions — a live 2 Hz scan, a wall-bounded 1200 mm arena, and an origin file (fpms_teleop_origin.json). Let the operator drag the ghost rover until the scan's walls line up with the arena border, then commit the new origin.
why: This converts the project's worst property — an unfixable accumulating drift — into a RECOVERABLE one, and it makes every other pose-dependent feature (cross-track error, distance-to-next, occupancy) worth building. It also directly addresses the recurring operational failure in ODO-006: a stale origin once put the rover at (-9182, -11926) mm inside a 1200 mm arena, and the current remedy is a re-zeroing ritual a human must remember after every boot. Complements rather than duplicates the automatic wall fix (OPS-015): the human eye does the alignment, so it does not require the mount yaw to be calibrated to <0.5 deg first. CAVEAT: it shares the M6 precondition — if there are no physical walls to see, there is no alignment cue — and an operator aligning a MIRRORED scan (OPS-016) in a square arena could still commit a wrong pose.

claim: ADD A YAW CONE to the heading ray. RViz draws a cone for 2-D pose orientation uncertainty precisely because a single heading ray OVERSTATES CONFIDENCE; it draws position covariance as a 2-sigma ellipsoid from the eigendecomposition of the 3x3 block ('eigenvalues are the variances, so we take the sqrt to draw the standard deviation' x2). Our heading ray is already dashed when assumed, but a shallow wedge either side of it, widening with accumulated turn, says the same thing quantitatively.
why: Pairs with the modelled drift ring (R3-006): the ring bounds position, the cone bounds heading, and heading is the term that matters most here because 1 degree of heading error is 17.5 mm of lateral error over a 1 m leg (R2-009). Both are declared models rather than measurements and must be labelled as such.

claim: The planned route renders IDENTICALLY before, during and after execution — progress along a route is currently unrepresented. Add active-leg highlighting (current leg 2 px full opacity, rest 1.5 px/60%, completed stepped down further), waypoint NUMBERS matching the mission strip's leg list, and one direction CHEVRON per leg. On a 1200 mm arena an operator otherwise cannot tell whether a route runs out-and-back or back-and-out.
why: Directly serves the multi-leg ROUTES feature (MIS-004): 'leg 2 failed' should point at a specific numbered dot. R3 stresses KEEPING the existing draw order — the in-code comment 'a plan is intent; everything else on this canvas is measurement, and measurement should never be obscured by intent' matches Nav2's own global-plan/local-plan layering and must not be changed.

claim: Draw a hairline perpendicular from the rover glyph to the active leg and print the CROSS-TRACK ERROR in mm next to the badge. It is the single number that reveals dead reckoning coming apart, and it costs one point-to-segment projection per frame. Also add distance-to-next ('NEXT WP · 340 mm'), which Mission Planner computes per-leg for exactly this reason.
why: Cross-track error is the operator-visible early warning for the drift that R2-009 proves is unbounded. It is the UI counterpart to the twist-versus-pose disagreement counter in fpms_odom_tf.py (ODO-004): a cheap continuously-displayed number that catches a developing fault without anyone running a test.

claim: Adopt a THREE-STATE ARMING LADDER, not a boolean: SAFE (no motion possible) -> ARMED (mission may start) -> RUNNING, mirroring PX4's Disarmed/Prearmed/Armed. The intermediate state is what makes 'armed but not moving' a visible, deliberate state. Put the blocking reasons INSIDE the arm control, in ArduPilot's literal one-line format: 'PreArm: LiDAR not publishing', 'PreArm: pose never reported', 'PreArm: link down 12s', 'PreArm: rover not in start box'. Ship advisory first; make it enforcing once the checks are trustworthy.
why: The project already HAS the refusal logic and the reasons — the mission refuses to start when the obstacle guard is blind (OPS-002) and the nav2 backend refuses with a specific named missing link (MIS-002). This surfaces those existing refusals in the UI instead of leaving them in logs, which is why it is cheap: the checks exist, only the presentation is missing.

claim: CONFIRM MOTION WITH A GESTURE, NOT A MODAL — QGC's 'Slide to confirm operation' with hold-spacebar / X-cancel. This beats 'Are you sure?' because it is EFFORTFUL AND CONTINUOUS, so habituated click-through cannot complete it; NN/g is explicit that a bare confirmation is worse than nothing ('the only sensible reaction is of course I want to do the thing I just told you to do' and 'if you cry wolf too many times, people will stop paying attention'). Separately, hold-to-drive teleop must cancel on pointerup, pointercancel, BLUR, VISIBILITYCHANGE and a heartbeat gap — modern enabling devices are three-position (OFF-ON-OFF) because operators clench under stress.
why: Motion on this rover is never gentle (FW-002: there is no gentle duty), so an accidental start is never a small mistake — which is exactly why the effort belongs in the gesture. The blur/visibilitychange cases matter concretely: the existing 0.6 s jog deadman in fpms_teleop.py protects against a lost link, but not against an operator tabbing away with a pointer still down.

claim: Raw LiDAR points carry four classes by HUE ALONE on ~2 px squares — identity by colour at the size where hue perception is weakest, and the one place the map violates the never-colour-alone rule. Preferred fix: drop class colouring on raw points entirely, render them one recessive grey, and let the tracked-object BOXES carry class (they already encode shape: circle for TREE, filled rect for OBSTACLE, unfilled for wall). That shape encoding is load-bearing and must never be removed. Also add a hard cutoff at ~8 s that stops drawing the cloud entirely rather than fading forever.
why: Matches how Nav2/RViz layer raw returns underneath and semantics on top. The hard cutoff mirrors the project's own LID-004 principle exactly: a faint picture is still a picture and operators plan against it, which is the same reason the bridge stops publishing rather than repeating. R3 also recommends NOT adding an occupancy grid despite it being the better small-card form — a 2 Hz single-plane scan with a drifting pose would smear; revisit only if localisation lands.

claim: The map labels ticks 0..120 on both axes but draws NOTHING at (0,0). Add a small '0,0' corner glyph with two short axis arrows (-> +X, ^ +Y) at the bottom-left — static-layer work, free per frame. Add a pointer-move coordinate readout ('X 742 mm · Y 318 mm'), throttled to pointer events and written to a ref. Snap only where a snap is TRUE (region centroids, start-box centre, 100 mm major intersections), because free-form 1 mm placement is sub-pixel precision the operator cannot see and the rover cannot achieve. Do NOT add pan/zoom, and never allow view rotation.
why: The map claims cm-level precision but offers no way to interrogate a location, and with the origin unmarked the bottom-left convention (CRD-001) lives only in a comment — which is precisely the ambiguity the ZONE NAMING TRAP (UI-002) warns about. Snapping here is honesty, not convenience: the rover's motion quantum (R1-009) is far coarser than 1 mm.

claim: Two accessibility gaps remain open: the canvas has NO TEXT ALTERNATIVE (add an aria-live='polite' visually-hidden summary such as 'Rover at X 620 mm, Y 180 mm, heading 090 deg, pose assumed, scan 0.4 s old', rebuilt on the same 2 Hz message edge as the HUD strings), and the map has >=2 series (plan, trail, three point classes, three zones) with NO LEGEND anywhere — add a collapsed one-row key beneath the card with swatch + shape + word.
why: The on-map plates are direct labels that SUPPLEMENT a legend, not replace it. The aria-live summary is the map-adapted form of the 'a table view exists' requirement, and it reuses the existing 2 Hz HUD rebuild so it costs no extra per-frame work.

claim: VALIDATED REPLACEMENT SET for the dynamic layer, computed against our real arena floor '#0b0f16' with --pairs all: plan '#3987e5', driven '#f97316', assumed '#fbbf24', tree '#199e70'. All four pass the chroma floor (>=0.1), CVD separation (worst pair dE 8.5 protan against a >=8 target), normal-vision floor (worst dE 17.4 against a >=15 floor) and contrast vs surface (all >=3:1). Only the lightness-band check deviates, for the same accepted reason as the zones — our floor is far darker than the reference surface.
why: Reserve categorical hues for things that MOVE AND CHANGE and let the static regions keep carrying identity by glyph + bracket + label, which they already do. Note the driven path being the ember brand accent is deliberate — the thing that actually happened deserves the accent. CAVEAT: this set assumes R3's stale Defect 2 (R3-003); reconcile against the current emerald trailMeasured before applying, and re-run the validator for --mode light against '#ffffff' before shipping the light table.

claim: COMMAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: QGC surfaces 'Vehicle did not respond to command: <CMD>' on ACK timeout and treats unacknowledged as FAILED, not optimistically successful. Lock the control while a command is in flight and name the specific command in the failure. Separately, hard-separate authoring from commanding (QGC Plan View vs Fly View): the console should never allow editing a route while it is executing.
why: Treating unacknowledged as failed is the UI expression of the project's own norm that a refusal beats a plausible guess (OPS-012, MIS-002). It matters more here than on a drone because the link is the WiFi that OPS-002 shows swinging to -78 dBm: commands genuinely do go missing, and an optimistic UI would show a mission proceeding that never started.
